nutshell: Individually re-identifying honey bees in the field usually needs multi-color paint codes or extensive training data. This paper shows that a single dot of paint plus off-the-shelf vision foundation models (SAM2 for background removal, DINOv3 for embeddings) can support one-shot re-identification - training a lightweight ReID head from just one reference track per bee - reaching 86% top-1 accuracy across 45 identities.
contributions: A new dataset of 9,495 image crops across 45 red-paint-marked honey bee identities (358 tracks, avg 24.1 images/track), collected outdoors at a bee feeder with realistic pose/illumination variation, released publicly.

A one-shot ReID pipeline (pose-based cropping + SAM2 background removal + frozen foundation-model backbone + lightweight ArcFace-trained ReID head) that needs only a single reference track per identity, evaluated across 6 different foundation-model backbones (DINOv2, DINOv3, BioCLIPv1/v2, MegaDescriptor, an insect-specific foundation model).

Ablations isolating the effect of pose rectification, background masking, backbone size/resolution, and local (thorax/abdomen) vs. global (class) token selection on ReID accuracy, including a token-level similarity-map analysis showing the ReID head learns to suppress background/leg/wing regions and concentrate on the paint mark.
deficiencies: The scope is explicitly restricted to a single paint color (red) with only 45 IDs from one feeder over 3 days; the paper itself defers multi-color scaling to future work, so the demonstrated identity capacity is far below what a deployed multi-color system would need.

The headline 'best' result (thorax+class token concatenation, 88.5% top-1, Sec. 5.3) is reported as the top configuration, but the paper's own paired t-test finds no significant difference between it and the simpler thorax-token-only configuration - the paper still frames the concatenated variant as the standout result.

The cross-dataset comparison against prior work (Table 1, Flowerpatch Painted Bees) presents the ResNet+SCL baseline only at 'full' training data (0.98) with dashes for its 1-track/2-track rows - implying that baseline was never actually run in a matched one-shot/few-shot setting, so the claim of beating it with '10x less data' compares their 2-tracks/ID number against the baseline's only reported (full-data) number, not a like-for-like low-data comparison.

All evaluation is on a single species, one camera setup, and one paint color; no test of robustness to different paint colors, marking styles, or multi-day/multi-camera deployment drift is included despite the paper motivating the work around realistic field deployment.
notable: A background-only patch token (containing zero bee pixels after masking) still achieves 11% top-1 ReID accuracy - over 5x random chance for 45 classes - revealing that DINOv3's local patch tokens retain leaked global/positional information even for empty patches; the paper uses this finding responsibly to contextualize (rather than overstate) its local-token results. Also notable: BioCLIPv1 outperforming its own successor BioCLIPv2 by ~6% is flagged as a genuine, somewhat counterintuitive negative result about scaling species-classification training data for a fine-grained individual-ID task.
